turns.U1:
In inflection, titleize mangles acronyms: titleize('NASA rocket launch') returns 'Nasa Rocket Launch' and titleize('read the HTTP spec') returns 'Read The Http Spec'. Can you make titleize keep all-caps acronyms like NASA and HTTP as they are?

The repo is checked out (as a git working copy) at /home/user/cs_workspaces/CS-03/inflection. Code from the repo can't be run directly on this machine; use the two wrapper scripts, which run it in an isolated container: /home/user/cs_workspaces/CS-03/run_tests.sh [pytest args] (e.g. run_tests.sh -q tests) and /home/user/cs_workspaces/CS-03/run_python.sh -c '...'. Please keep all your work inside /home/user/cs_workspaces/CS-03.
turns.U2: Thanks. Two refinements: if the whole input is already in uppercase (like a shouted heading 'HELLO WORLD'), titleize should still produce 'Hello World' like it does today - only treat an all-caps word as an acronym when the input also contains lowercase letters. And please don't change the behaviour of humanize() or underscore() themselves; other code relies on them (for example humanize('employee_salary') must stay 'Employee salary', and underscore('NASARocket') must stay exactly what it returns now).
turns.clarification_reply: Please go ahead with your best judgment.

intended_requirements.statement: When the input contains lowercase letters, all-caps words of two or more letters are kept as-is: titleize('NASA rocket launch') == 'NASA Rocket Launch'; titleize('read the HTTP spec') == 'Read The HTTP Spec'.
If the entire input is uppercase, titleize behaves as before: titleize('HELLO WORLD') == 'Hello World'.
humanize() output is unchanged for all inputs (e.g. humanize('employee_salary') == 'Employee salary', humanize('author_id') == 'Author').
underscore() output is unchanged for all inputs (e.g. underscore('NASARocket') returns what it returns at the base commit).

unscored_or_ambiguous: Single capital letters ('A', 'I') as acronyms: not specified; titleize('TheManWithoutAPast') keeping 'The Man Without A Past' is covered by the regression norm only.
Acronyms embedded in CamelCase input (e.g. 'HTTPServer'), words with digits ('MP3'), and mixed-case words ('iPhone') are not specified.
